text:
anna: Heads up — we're onboarding ModelCruft-3B_v0.9 for a customer POC. License file in the repo has a weird "inference-only" / "no redistribution of weights" clause. We want to quantize and let the customer run the model in their VPC. Is that a no-go? :thinking:
samir: Can you paste the exact clause? sometimes 'inference-only' means you can't ship checkpoints but can run in customer's infra if we host it. confusing wording often.
anna: pasted the license excerpt below:

```
ModelCruft License v1.0
You are permitted to use the model for research and commercial inference.
Redistribution of model checkpoint files, binary weights, or any derivative weight files is prohibited unless explicitly permitted by the upstream licensor.
Derivative models (trained or quantized variants) may be created for internal use only; any distribution to third parties requires prior written permission and attribution.
Attribution: include "ModelCruft-3B_v0.9 (ModelCruft Labs)" in product documentation.
```

marc: Thanks. That looks pretty restrictive — the line "distribution to third parties requires prior written permission" likely covers shipping quantized weights to a customer. A few notes:
- Quantized weights are "derivative weight files" under that text.
- Running the model inside a customer-managed VPC where we give them the weights would be redistribution.
- Hosting the model behind an API (we host, they call) is usually ok if license allows inference.

taylor: +1 to marc. We should treat this as "inference-only" unless we obtain an explicit redistribution waiver. Also the required attribution is straightforward but doesn't cure the redistribution prohibition.

anna: Ok — for the POC the customer needs on-prem inference (air-gapped). They want the binary to deploy. If redistribution is disallowed we can't provide it without permission.

samir: Short-term workaround: offer to deploy in their environment ourselves (managed install) without handing over weights. For longer term, we'd need upstream permission or a commercial license.

marc: Action items:
1) legal to draft a vendor clarification email / request for redistribution addendum.
2) eng to gather provenance (model card, exact hash of weights, model training data attribution) and test quantization internally to measure fidelity loss.
3) product to align on ask we make (NDA, commercial terms).

ops-bot: Suggestion: collect files and checksums with this command:
```
curl -sL https://modelrepo.example.com/ModelCruft-3B_v0.9/license.txt -o license.txt
sha256sum model-weights.bin > weights.sha256
```

anna: I'll attach the repo link and checksum in the ticket. Also worth noting the license wants the attribution string in product docs — we'll need to bake that into the onboarding checklist.

samir: Another angle: some licensors allow distribution of quantized/PRUNED weights under an explicit clause. We can ask upstream: "Can we distribute quantized INT8 weights to enterprise customers under a paid addendum?" If yes, we should require a signed addendum per customer.

marc: Exactly. Draft template language for the ask — include: permission to distribute quantized/converted weights, permitted destinations (customer-owned infra vs third-party cloud), required attribution language, and any embargo/usage restrictions.

anna: Can someone draft the vendor message? I'll iterate with legal. Draft below — feel free to edit:

```
Hi ModelCruft team,
We're evaluating ModelCruft-3B_v0.9 for a paid enterprise POC. The license mentions redistribution restrictions for "derivative weight files". Could you clarify whether quantized weights (e.g., INT8) may be redistributed to a customer under a commercial addendum or if we must only host inference via API/managed install? If redistribution is allowed, please include any required attribution or downstream license text.
Thanks,
Anna (Redwood Inference)
```

marc: Good start. I'll add a short legal paragraph about a typical addendum (scope, duration, revocation, audit rights).

taylor: Also ask them to confirm whether the "attribution" text is sufficient as-is or must be included in end-user docs, UIs, and/or privacy policies. Some licensors require prominent attribution.

anna: Cool. For now we'll mark POC as "hosted-managed only" until we get explicit permission. I'll file the ticket and tag legal + product. :thumbsup:

samir: One more thing — if upstream denies redistribution, we should evaluate alternative models that have explicit commercial redistribution clauses. I can run a quick cost/latency comparison for replacements.

marc: Agree. TL;DR: Not safe to ship quantized weights to customers without permission. Proceed with managed hosting or get an addendum. I'll open a vendor outreach ticket now.

ops-bot: Ticket created: INF-2026-4512 — "ModelCruft redistribution clarification". Assigned to marc, anna, samir, taylor.

anna: Thanks everyone. I'll update the POC doc and add the attribution checklist item. :eyes:
